articles.title: Juan Francisco Casas Studio / Positive Livings
english: Juan Francisco Casas Studio's latest project, Positive Livings, completed in 2025 in Madrid, Spain, redefines urban living by embracing outdoor spaces. The design incorporates the concept of bringing daily activities into the public realm, effectively enriching the social fabric of the neighborhood.

The architects emphasize the importance of community interaction, encouraging residents to bring their daily routines outdoors. This idea harkens back to simpler times when neighbors gathered on the streets, fostering connections and a sense of belonging.

Positive Livings challenges the conventional notions of private and public spaces, creating a seamless blend of home and street. Such innovative designs not only enhance the quality of life for inhabitants but also contribute to a vibrant urban environment.
chinese: 胡安·弗朗西斯科·卡薩斯工作室最新項目《積極生活空間》於2025年在西班牙馬德里完工，重新定義城市生活，擁抱戶外空間。設計概念是將日常活動引入公共領域，實質上豐富了社區的社會結構。
建築師強調社區互動的重要性，鼓勵居民將日常生活搬到戶外。這一理念追溯到更簡單的時代，鄰居們聚集在街道上，促進了聯繫和歸屬感。
《積極生活空間》挑戰了對私密空間和公共空間的傳統觀念，創造了家庭與街道的無縫融合。這樣的創新設計不僅提高了居民的生活質量，還為城市環境增添了活力。

articles.title: ARO transforms Green-Wood Cemetery greenhouse in New York into welcome centre
english: ARO, a New York architecture studio, has rejuvenated a historic greenhouse at Green-Wood Cemetery in Brooklyn, enhancing it with a new welcome center and courtyard. The renovation supports the cemetery's expanded operations while preserving its 19th-century aesthetic, demonstrating the studio's commitment to maintaining historical integrity amidst modern needs.

Originally built in the late 19th century as a flower shop for the cemetery, the greenhouse fell into disrepair until the cemetery administration consolidated its welcome services at this site. The design features a burgundy-colored building that complements the existing greenhouse, aimed at making the venue welcoming for both visitors and the community.

The project also emphasizes landscaping, which visually connects the new structures with the cemetery's greenery. ARO's approach highlights accessibility and inclusivity, ensuring that the greenhouse serves as a cherished space for both the living and the deceased, ultimately linking the cemetery to the surrounding neighborhood.
chinese: ARO，一家位於紐約的建築工作室，已經重振布魯克林綠木公墓內的一座歷史溫室，並以全新的迎賓中心和庭院進行加強改造。這項翻新支持了公墓擴展業務的需求，同時保留了19世紀的美學，展現了該工作室在現代需求中保持歷史完整性的承諾。
這座溫室最初建於19世紀末，曾作為公墓的花店，但在公墓管理局將其迎賓服務整合到這個地點之前，它已經荒廢。設計中融合了一座深紅色建築，以補充現有的溫室，旨在為訪客和社區創造一個友好的場域。
該項目還強調了景觀設計，視覺上將新結構與公墓的綠意連接起來。ARO的設計理念強調可進入性和包容性，確保這座溫室成為生者和逝者珍視的空間，並最終將墓地與周邊社區聯繫起來。

articles.topic: Oratory Chapel by S-AR: A Study in Memory and Material Reuse
articles.title: thin concrete walls frame tiny chapel by S-AR, built from its own remains
english: The Oratory Chapel, designed by S-AR, elegantly blends with its surroundings in Santiago, Nuevo León, Mexico, while reinterpreting an earlier chapel that once occupied the site. The design emphasizes the innovative use of thin concrete walls that manipulate height and light, creating an engaging spatial experience. By reusing elements from the original structure, the chapel establishes a continuity that honors its historical context and enhances its narrative.

The structure is defined by two reinforced concrete walls, each only 8 cm thick, which rise at varying heights and support a narrow concrete slab. This configuration leads to a tunnel-like interior space, while strategically placed openings invite light and air, softening the otherwise stark environment. Inside, a wooden bench adds warmth, contrasting with the concrete, and a geometric iron cross reinforces the spatial boundary, further linking the new design to its predecessor.

This project by S-AR exemplifies thoughtful architecture that merges memory and modernity. By reassembling materials from the past in a new configuration, the chapel not only retains the essence of its history but also presents a fresh architectural identity. The Oratory Chapel stands as a compact intervention that invites visitors to reflect on the interplay between materiality, memory, and site.
chinese: S-AR設計的Oratory Chapel巧妙地融入墨西哥新莱昂州圣地亚哥的環境，同時重新詮釋了曾經位於該地點的早期小教堂。這一設計強調了薄混凝土牆的創新運用，通過操控高度和光線，創造出引人入勝的空間體驗。通過重用原有結構的元素，小教堂建立起尊重歷史背景的連貫性，增強了其敘事性。
這座結構由兩面每面厚度僅8公分的加強混凝土牆界定，這些牆沿著對角線不規則上升，並支撐著一片狹窄的混凝土板。這樣的配置導致了一個隧道形內部空間，而有策略地設置的開口則邀請光線和空氣進入，柔化了原本生硬的環境。室內，一張木製長椅增添了溫暖感，與混凝土形成對比，幾何形狀的鐵十字架則強化了空間的邊界，進一步將新設計與其前身聯繫起來。
此S-AR的項目展示了融合記憶與現代性的周到建築設計。通過將過去的材料重新組合成新配置，小教堂不僅保留了歷史的精髓，還呈現出全新的建築身份。Oratory Chapel作為一個緊湊的介入，邀請參觀者反思材料性、記憶和場地之間的相互作用。
